- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp spike in true price (e.g., >20% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should be adjusted upward by 5–15% to reflect momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment swings sharply, adjust forecast to align with sentiment’s direction and magnitude.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underperform; increase forecast by 15–25% for next 7–14 days to compensate for low sentiment bias.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; if sentiment changes by >0.33 in 2–3 days, adjust forecast to reflect gradual adjustment rather than abrupt change.
